analysis.title: The Fed is only taking a break
key_insights: The Fed left the fed funds target range unchanged at 3.75%-4.00% on 28 October 2026, as expected, following a rate hike at its previous meeting.
Two FOMC members dissented in favor of a hike: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and, for the first time, Governor Lisa Cook.
The statement was slightly revised and now describes economic growth as 'strong', up from 'solid'. Commerzbank expects Q3 real GDP growth above 3% q/q annualized, due the next day.

The Fed said it is holding to gather further information to ensure a swift return of inflation to the 2% target. Commerzbank says inflation has been above target for more than five and a half years and has drifted further away in recent months.
Commerzbank expects September PCE inflation at 3.6% headline and 3.1% core.
Chair Warsh said the 2% target is not a 'soft target', but gave no specific timeline and declined to comment on future decisions. Commerzbank found his explanation for not hiking unconvincing.
Commerzbank argues the lack of Fed guidance may lead the market to price a higher uncertainty premium.
Commerzbank expects data before the next meeting to show persistently high inflation and forecasts a 25bp rate hike in December.

Process changes: the Fed keeps eight regular meetings a year, but one 2027 meeting will be devoted to monetary policy strategy with no rate decision expected, and two of eight in 2028 will focus on strategy. The Productivity Task Force, one of five set up by Warsh, holds a hearing on November 16 with Warsh participating.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Rates held after the prior meeting's hike. Two dissents favored a further hike, which shows a hawkish tilt inside the committee.
Commerzbank expects the release due 29 October to confirm the Fed's 'strong' growth description.
Commerzbank forecast. Inflation is moving further above the 2% target.
Commerzbank forecast. Core inflation is also drifting away from target.
Commerzbank's call for the next meeting, based on expected persistently high inflation data.

risk_factors: Inflation has been above the Fed's 2% target for more than five and a half years and is drifting further away.
Weak Fed communication and guidance could raise the market's uncertainty premium.
The Fed's rationale for pausing despite strong growth and elevated inflation is unclear, which raises policy path uncertainty.
